domain.name: Frontend Engineering
domain.description: Deep mastery of browser internals, rendering, and client application architecture.

topic.title: Browser Rendering
topic.description: How browsers turn HTML, CSS, and JS into pixels on screen.

learning_sessions.title: Critical Rendering Path
learning_sessions.objective: Explain the steps browsers take to convert HTML/CSS into rendered pixels, and identify which steps a given code change affects.
learning_sessions.content:
The critical rendering path is the sequence of steps a browser takes to convert HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into pixels on screen: 1) Parse HTML into the DOM. 2) Parse CSS into the CSSOM. 3) Combine DOM + CSSOM into the render tree (visible nodes only). 4) Layout: compute the size and position of every render tree node. 5) Paint: fill in pixels for text, color, images, borders, shadows. 6) Composite: combine painted layers in the correct order, using the GPU where possible.

Changes that only affect paint (e.g. background-color) are cheaper than changes that trigger layout (e.g. width, font-size), because layout invalidates everything downstream of it. CSS properties like `transform` and `opacity` can be composited without touching layout or paint, which is why animating them is preferred for smooth 60fps animations.

exercises.prompt: You change a button's `background-color` on hover. Which critical-rendering-path step is the most expensive one this change triggers?

options: Paint only, for the button's pixels
CSSOM re-parse of the entire stylesheet
definition.explanation: background-color doesn't change any element's size or position, so layout is skipped entirely; the browser only has to repaint the button's own pixels.
